title: The Dancing Plague of 1518: A Chilling Case of Mass Hysteria
actual_content_summary: In 1518, hundreds of people in Strasbourg, France, mostly women, began dancing uncontrollably in the streets, ignoring exhaustion and heat, with some eventually dying from the exertion. The cause of this 'dancing plague' remains a mystery, with theories including a toxic fungus and mass hysteria, but it is believed to have been driven by deep-seated psychological needs for release and connection. The incident is a reminder of the power of mass hysteria and the thin line between sanity and madness.
